sections.body:
A **day** is one whole turn of the earth. It has a morning, an afternoon, an evening and a night. The sun comes up, we play and learn, we eat, and then we sleep.

A day has parts, and each part has its own feel. In the **morning** it is bright and people are busy. In the **afternoon** the sun is high and we play or do our homework. In the **evening** the light turns orange and the family comes home together. At **night** it is dark and quiet and we rest.

The **calendar** tells you the day of the week. A week has seven days, and the days always come in the same order.

A day also has hours. There are 24 hours in a day, and they are numbered from 0 to 23. When people say ‘meet me at 7’, they usually mean 7 in the morning. When they say ‘at 19’, they mean 7 in the evening.

When you know the parts of a day, you can tell a story about your own day. And you can tell what comes next.
examples: This is my day. I get up at six.
In the morning I eat breakfast.
In the afternoon I do my homework.
sections.heading: What is a day?

sections.body:
Most mornings look the same. That is a good thing, because a familiar morning is easy.

First, my alarm rings and I wake up. I stretch and sit up.

Next, I go to the bathroom and wash my face and brush my teeth.

Then I get dressed. I put on my clothes and my shoes by the door.

After that, we have breakfast together. I eat, and I talk with my family about the day.

Finally, I pack my bag and say goodbye. Then I go to school, or I play with my friends.

If you make this order your own, the morning gets easy. You know what comes next, and nothing feels rushed.
examples: I brush my teeth before breakfast.
I eat breakfast with my mum.
sections.heading: How my morning goes
steps: Wake up when the alarm rings and stretch.
Wash your face and brush your teeth.
Get dressed and put your shoes by the door.
Pack your bag and say goodbye.

sections.body:
The afternoon is the busy middle of the day.

After school I have lunch. Then I do my homework. Homework is the school work you finish at home.

After that, I play. I ride my bike, or I play in the yard with my neighbours. Somebody has to watch me at the street, so I play where a grown-up can see me.

At about five o'clock the light changes. This is the **evening**. The sky turns orange, then grey. This is the time when people come home from work.

In the evening we eat dinner together. It is the best part of the day for many families, because everyone is there.

After dinner we have a quiet time. I read a book, or I draw. Some families watch a programme together. Some children help wash the dishes.

Then comes **bedtime**. I brush my teeth again, I put on my pyjamas, and I read one more book in bed.
examples: After school I do my homework.
We eat dinner together at six.
In the evening I read a story before bed.
sections.heading: My afternoon and my evening

sections.body:
These are the words for the people you live with and the parts of the day.

Morning is the part of the day from when you wake up until lunchtime.

Noon is the middle of the day, around twelve o'clock.

Evening is after the afternoon, when the light gets soft and people come home.

A **mother** is the woman who looks after you. Some children have more than one mother in their family, and that is fine too.

A **father** is the man who looks after you. A **grandmother** is your father's or mother's mother.

Bedtime is the time when you go to bed. Every family has its own bedtime, and it is usually earlier on a school night.
sections.heading: Words for our family and our day

terms.example: In the morning I drink a glass of milk.
terms.gloss: The part of the day from when you wake up until lunchtime.
The middle of the day, around twelve o'clock. It is also called midday.
The part of the day after the afternoon. The light gets soft and people come home.

terms.example: My mother works at a shop in the market.
terms.gloss: The woman who looks after you and lives with you.

terms.example: My bedtime is nine o'clock on school nights.
terms.gloss: The time when you stop playing and go to bed.

sections.body:
A **family** is the people who belong to you and look after you. Families look different all over the world, and that is fine.

Some families have a father, a mother and children. Some have one parent. Some have a grandmother or an uncle living with them. Some children have two families, one with each parent. Every one of these is a family.

Each person in a family has their own job. One person cooks. One person goes to work. One person drives the children to school. Someone is always in charge of the money.

Children have jobs too, and these are the good ones. Set the table. Put your shoes away. Feed the dog. Water the plants. Keep your own room tidy. Small jobs show that you are part of the family.

And family is not only the people at home. Your friends at school are a kind of family too. They help you, and you help them.
examples: This is my family. We live together.
I help my mother set the table.
sections.heading: The people in my family

sections.body:
A family works because everybody helps a little.

In the morning, someone makes breakfast and someone finds your shoes. At school, your teacher helps you learn. In the evening, someone cooks and someone washes up.

You can help in small ways. You can tidy your own things. You can bring your family water. You can listen when someone is sad.

Helping is not about being the fastest or the strongest. It is about noticing what someone else needs, and doing that thing.

And when you are tired or sad, the family helps you. That is what a family is for. If something is hard, you do not have to carry it alone.

Try it tonight. Find one small job that nobody asked you to do, and do it. Then see how the evening feels.
examples: I help my dad water the plants.
Can I help you carry the bag?
I will tidy my own things.
sections.heading: How we help each other

item.summary: Every day has a shape: morning, afternoon, evening, night. After reading this, you can put the parts of a day in order, name the people in your family and what they do, and say what happens at each time of day.
item.title: A Day in My Family
